text:
rachel: quick flag 7 - ran PTQ build of new reranker (rankfast-2b-ptq) on two benchmarks and seeing a weird split: NDCG@10 up ~1.5% on web-search but MRR@5 down ~4% on support-docs. seems concentrated on medium docs (200-500 tokens).

ton y: can you share the run command + which quant backend? per-tensor vs per-channel makes a big diff for layernorm/ffn.

rachel: used our standard pipeline: `tools/quantize.py --model rankfast-2b --backend onnxruntime --mode ptq --calib=1024` then `./eval_rerank.py --model rankfast-2b-ptq --queries support_queries_mid.jsonl --candidates cand_support.jsonl --truncate 512 --seed 7 --batch 128 --tokenizer redwood-tokenizer`.

priya: odd that NDCG moves in the other direction. could be candidate distribution in web-search is more forgiving (topk patterns) while support-docs penalizes top1 swaps. do you have score distributions and pairwise swap counts?

rachel: pasted numbers:
- web-search: NDCG@10 fp16 0.814 -> ptq 0.827, MRR@5 0.642 -> 0.638
- support-docs: NDCG@10 fp16 0.752 -> 0.749, MRR@5 0.711 -> 0.683

- score stats (support mid): fp16 mean 1.05 std 0.30, ptq mean 0.98 std 0.16
- pairwise top1 swaps (1k samples): 82 swaps increased where ptq moved wrong doc above correct one.

ton y: std collapse again. looks like compressed logits after quantization. which ops were quantized? LayerNorm and final `dense_out`? sometimes fake-quant on layernorm scale/bias kills calibration.

rachel: yes we quant'd LayerNorm, matmuls and final dense. we used default op list. export logs show `fold_bias=False` for layernorm but `fold_bias=True` for linear. maybe layernorm bias left floating.

priya: if layernorm bias isn't folded you can get mean shift. also check if we used symmetric vs asymmetric quant for small tensors. per-channel probably better for final dense.

(eval-bot): job 6340001300 started: re-run sweep with (A) per-channel quant for weights, (B) fold_layernorm_bias=True, (C) post-quant ptq-calib-size=4096.

rachel: running those now. also adding an ablation (D) where we re-apply a tiny calibration scale to final logits: multiply by 1.1 post-hoc to see if it recovers MRR.

(eval-bot): job 6340001450 finished: outputs uploaded `/tmp/ptq-sweep-support/*`

rachel: results:
- A (per-channel): MRR@5 = 0.693 (big improvement), NDCG@10 ~0.750
- B (fold_layernorm_bias=True): MRR@5 = 0.701, NDCG@10 ~0.751
- C (calib-size=4096): marginal gain MRR@5 = 0.688
- D (post-scale 1.1): MRR@5 = 0.690

priya: wow per-channel + fold bias basically fixes it. suggests weight quantization granularity was main culprit and layernorm bias folding amplified mean shift.

ton y: two action items: 1) change default PTQ config to per-channel for linear weights, 2) ensure export pipeline folds layernorm bias by default. also add a quick stats check in onboarding: compare std(logits) vs fp16 baseline and fail if std drop > 0.12.

rachel: agreed. i'll open PR that updates `infra/quant/defaults.yaml` and `tools/export_onnx.py` to enable `fold_layernorm_bias` and per-channel quant by default for linear matmuls.

ops-bot: scheduled bench job (wkly-regression) will pick up the new quant build tomorrow at 03:15 UTC.

priya: also consider adding tiny calibration retrain (1 epoch on calibration set) to recover small distributional shifts automatically. we did this before for other models.

rachel: yep adding note to onboarding checklist and adding a tiny optional `calib_retrain: true` flag to the quant pipeline.

ton y: can we also add a smoke evaluation that runs both web-search and support-docs mid-slice and asserts: `MRR@5 >= baseline - 0.03 OR (per-channel && fold_layernorm_bias)`? basically allow opt-in fallback but alert on drift.

rachel: will add smoke. PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/407 — includes default config changes, small eval smoke, and updated export logs. tagging you both.

priya: nice triage. follow-up: let's record the numeric heuristics in model-onboard docs (std thresholds, pairwise-swap limits) so future quant ops don't silently regress user-facing MRR.

rachel: adding to docs now. closing thread once PR merges. thanks :rocket:
